answer: A 2019 base year must be recalculated under the GHG Protocol structural-change rule: remove the divested grain trade (Baltic sold 10 Mar 2022, Finnish 31 May 2022) from 2019 Scope 3 cat 1 as if it had never been owned, and add Foodhills (acquired 27 Nov 2025) for 2019 as if it had always been owned (own operations + ~300 SE pea growers in cat 1/FLAG). Published restatements (2022: 201,016 → 186,430 t; 2023: 260,931 → 237,886 t) show the grain-trade effect. Because Foodhills has no 2019 data, SBTi V2's preference for the most recent comprehensive year (2025, adjusted to full-year Foodhills) is the more defensible base; a 2019 base would require estimation and should be flagged as such. Pudasjärvi closure (2026) and Kantvik steam sale (2027) are later structural changes that also trigger recalculation checks.

answer: Rapeseed is not a relevant commodity under the EUDR (commodities: cattle, cocoa, coffee, palm oil, rubber, soya, wood), so rapeseed is out of scope. Soy is in scope, but only for products listed by HS code in Annex I (soybeans 1201, soy oil 1507, soy meal 2304). Soy protein isolate (HS 3504) is not listed, so the soy protein isolate in this dataset is not in EUDR scope — but it remains an SBTN high-impact commodity and a deforestation-risk exposure; Annex I can be amended by delegated act, so screening must be by HS code and re-checked.

answer: Yes, but optionally and conditionally. Under the GHG Protocol Land Sector and Removals Standard (v1.1, effective 1 Jan 2027) removals may be reported (they are optional) only if they are monitored with ongoing primary data, traceable to the specific land (parcels in the company's value chain), quantified with stated uncertainty, and with reversals accounted for (a reversal monitoring/permanence mechanism). Removals are reported separately from emissions, never netted into gross Scope 3. Catch-crop soil carbon gains are not modelled in this dataset and would need soil sampling/model-based MRV.

answer: Because the atmosphere sees no change: the same physical goods with the same production emissions are bought; only the estimation method changes (spend × EEIO average → supplier-specific PCF). Under the GHG Protocol this is a methodology change, which requires recalculating the base year (if significant) so that base and target years use comparable methods. Reporting it as a reduction would misstate progress against SBTi targets. In our pathway, lever L27 is shown as a measurement change with 0 t abatement.
